::: {.book-summary} ## Book Summary Insight Revelation unveils the ultimate triumph of God, the victory of Jesus Christ, the defeat of evil, and the fulfillment of God's redemptive plan. The book teaches that Christ reigns sovereignly over history, His people are called to faithful endurance, and God's kingdom will culminate in a new creation where He dwells forever with His redeemed people. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 1
Revelation 1:8
I am Alpha and Omega
### Why This Verse Foundational declaration of Christ's eternity ### Chapter Insight This chapter introduces the revelation given to John and presents the glorified Christ. The key verse emphasizes Jesus' sovereign authority over history, death, and the church. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 2
Revelation 2:10
Be thou faithful unto death
### Why This Verse One of Revelation's most quoted exhortations ### Chapter Insight This chapter contains messages to the churches of Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, and Thyatira. The key verse highlights Christ's call for faithfulness, repentance, and perseverance. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 3
Revelation 3:20
Behold, I stand at the door and knock
### Why This Verse Perhaps the most quoted verse in Revelation ### Chapter Insight This chapter contains messages to Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea. The key verse emphasizes spiritual vigilance, endurance, and wholehearted devotion to Christ. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 4
Revelation 4:11
Thou art worthy, O Lord
### Why This Verse Heavenly worship ### Chapter Insight This chapter transports John to heaven's throne room. The key verse reveals God's absolute sovereignty and worthiness of worship. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 5
Revelation 5:5
The Lion of the tribe of Judah
### Why This Verse Famous messianic title ### Chapter Insight This chapter presents the Lamb who alone is worthy to open the scroll. The key verse celebrates Christ's redemptive work and authority over God's purposes. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 6
Revelation 6:10
How long, O Lord?
### Why This Verse Cry of the martyrs ### Chapter Insight This chapter records the opening of the first six seals. The key verse demonstrates God's control over judgment, history, and human events. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 7
Revelation 7:17
God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes
### Why This Verse Comfort and restoration ### Chapter Insight This chapter reveals God's protection of His people and a vast multitude worshiping before His throne. The key verse highlights God's faithfulness to preserve and redeem His people from every nation. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 8
Revelation 8:1
There was silence in heaven
### Why This Verse Dramatic prophetic moment ### Chapter Insight This chapter opens the seventh seal and introduces the first four trumpet judgments. The key verse emphasizes that God's judgments proceed according to His sovereign plan and in response to the prayers of His people. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 9
Revelation 9:6
Men shall seek death, and shall not find it
### Why This Verse Judgment imagery ### Chapter Insight This chapter records the fifth and sixth trumpet judgments. The key verse highlights both the severity of judgment and humanity's continued refusal to repent. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 10
Revelation 10:11
Thou must prophesy again
### Why This Verse Continuing witness ### Chapter Insight This chapter presents the mighty angel and the little scroll. The key verse emphasizes God's certainty in fulfilling His purposes and the prophet's responsibility to proclaim His message. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 11
Revelation 11:15
The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord
### Why This Verse Major kingdom proclamation ### Chapter Insight This chapter records the ministry of the two witnesses and the sounding of the seventh trumpet. The key verse celebrates God's coming reign over all the kingdoms of the world. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 12
Revelation 12:11
They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb
### Why This Verse One of the most quoted victory verses ### Chapter Insight This chapter portrays the woman, the child, and the dragon. The key verse reveals the ongoing spiritual conflict between God's purposes and Satan's opposition. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 13
Revelation 13:18
Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast
### Why This Verse Most famous apocalyptic verse ### Chapter Insight This chapter introduces the beast from the sea and the beast from the earth. The key verse warns of deceptive worldly powers that oppose God and seek worship for themselves. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 14
Revelation 14:13
Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord
### Why This Verse Frequently used funeral text ### Chapter Insight This chapter presents the victorious Lamb, the faithful redeemed, and announcements of coming judgment. The key verse emphasizes perseverance and faithfulness among God's people. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 15
Revelation 15:3
Great and marvelous are Thy works
### Why This Verse Song of Moses and the Lamb ### Chapter Insight This chapter introduces the final bowl judgments and celebrates God's holiness and justice. The key verse emphasizes that God's judgments are righteous and worthy of worship. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 16
Revelation 16:15
Blessed is he that watches
### Why This Verse Call to readiness ### Chapter Insight This chapter records the pouring out of the seven bowl judgments. The key verse demonstrates the completion of God's wrath against persistent rebellion. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 17
Revelation 17:14
The Lamb shall overcome them
### Why This Verse Victory of Christ ### Chapter Insight This chapter describes the judgment of Babylon the Great. The key verse reveals the downfall of a corrupt world system opposed to God. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 18
Revelation 18:4
Come out of her, My people
### Why This Verse Separation from Babylon ### Chapter Insight This chapter continues Babylon's fall and calls God's people to separate from her sins. The key verse emphasizes the certainty of God's judgment upon worldly pride and corruption. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 19
Revelation 19:16
King of Kings and Lord of Lords
### Why This Verse One of Christ's greatest titles ### Chapter Insight This chapter celebrates heaven's praise, the marriage supper of the Lamb, and Christ's victorious return. The key verse presents Jesus as King of kings and Lord of lords. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 20
Revelation 20:12
The books were opened
### Why This Verse Final judgment ### Chapter Insight This chapter records Satan's final defeat, the Millennium, and the Great White Throne Judgment. The key verse highlights God's final victory over evil and the ultimate accountability of humanity. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 21
Revelation 21:4
God shall wipe away all tears
### Why This Verse One of the most beloved promises in Scripture ### Chapter Insight This chapter reveals the New Heaven, New Earth, and New Jerusalem. The key verse promises God's eternal presence with His people and the removal of all suffering. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 22
Revelation 22:13
I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end
### Why This Verse Final declaration of Christ ### Chapter Insight This chapter concludes with the river of life, final exhortations, and Christ's promise to return. The key verse expresses the believer's longing for Christ's coming and eternal fellowship with Him. :::
